main_body: Multi-storey brick facade with a flat green (grass/tiled) roof seen from above, topped by a light parapet and cream cornice
top_band: Green roof surface with a light grey/white parapet rim, rows ~3-38 (about 35 rows), speckled greens with two roof vents; the cream cornice at rows 42-46 marks the front edge
evidence: Down the middle column: light parapet rim, then a wide green roof plane with vents (a clear horizontal surface, 35 rows), then a pale parapet front edge and a cream cornice line at rows ~42-46. A dark shadow row follows, then the brick front face with floor bands. Windows have sills, lintels and dark inset glazing, and the arched door has a dark surround. The top is far more than a rim, and the front face is distinct, so the structure reads as 3/4.

style.evidence: The brick wall uses about 4-5 tones (dark mortar, mid and light reds, per-brick variation) with cream trim and a cornice. The roof has speckled greens in 4 steps with vents. Outlines are dark red-brown beside brick and dark green beside the roof, not black. The windows carry blue/white glazing detail. The pattern is repetitive, but it has no large flat fills, and it would sit acceptably next to the references, though slightly less rich than their tile roofs.
